kicker: An agent game platform, two scenes

steps.say: A valley you can walk through, where every cloud, mountain and blade of grass is drawn in code.
Claude Fable 5.2 helped build it, and it lives on a new platform called patch.

scenes.headline: patch, and two scenes built on it
scenes.sub: A painted valley and a coloured-pencil town, taken apart
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Mossby! The platform first, then both scenes, shader by shader.

steps.say: patch launched on November the ninth: a command line tool and an MCP server for coding agents, an asset library, and a host for games.

steps.caption: Search, git, release and test
steps.say: Its tools are search, git, release and test. None of them makes a mesh, a texture or a sound. Your agent still writes the game.

scenes.title: Where the library comes from
scenes.say: The library is real, and most of it is Kenney. Every item is public domain or Creative Commons with attribution, and carries its credit line.

scenes.title: From your agent's build to live

stations.label: Build
stations.sub: with the tools it already has

stations.label: Code scan
stations.sub: malware scan, then a model reads it

steps.say: Publishing is one command. Your agent builds the game with whatever it already has.
patch checks the files for secrets, size, and requests to other hosts.
Patch Desktop plays it once on your own Windows PC and records it.
Your agent watches that recording and says whether it starts and plays.

steps.term: Trust tier: sandboxed, game files only, or runs code
steps.say: Then a malware scan, and an AI model reads the code. With no warnings, no person looks at it.
And it is live.

scenes.title: Read before you install
scenes.say: Three things in the docs and terms are worth reading first.

items.text: The default licence keeps work on patch
items.say: A new repo starts under the Patch licence. You can read and remix it, but not take it off patch. Both scenes chose MIT instead.

items.text: Some mods launch with anti-cheat off
items.say: The terms say that for some games, patch starts the game with its anti-cheat off for that session, so mods can load.

items.text: The installer edits your agent's instructions
items.say: And the installer writes a use patch section into your global Claude and Codex instructions, then restores it on every update.

steps.say: Painted Valley is plain three dot js on WebGL two. It downloads 12.8 megabytes, and the scenery in it is code: the only pictures are two textures for the footpaths.

steps.caption: The one model: patch's starter figure
steps.say: The only model is the walker. The grass, trees, clouds, mountains and village are all written in code.

scenes.title: The paint finish, pixel by pixel

steps.term: Kuwahara: smooth the inside, keep the edges
steps.say: The finish is a Kuwahara filter. Here is a patch of the frame as pixels: two paints meeting at an edge, both speckled.
Around each pixel, take a small window and cut it into four overlapping quadrants.
Measure how much each quadrant varies. The calmest sits wholly on one side of the edge, and the pixel takes its mean.
Do that everywhere. Inside a region all four quadrants agree, so the speckle goes flat.
At the edge, one quadrant always stays on one side, so the edge survives. It looks like a loaded brush.

scenes.credit: the live page, finish off and on

steps.caption: Finish off
steps.say: In the valley, press P. Without the finish, the bushes are speckle.

steps.caption: Finish on
steps.say: With it, they are a few flat patches. The walker writes a low alpha, so the filter leaves him alone.

scenes.title: Two paints and a short step
scenes.say: Light on the walker is a step, not a gradient.

parts.say: Smoothstep rises from zero to one as the surface turns toward the sun.

parts.note: the turn is a few pixels wide
parts.say: Over a tiny width, so each part of him is two tones with a clean turn between.

parts.note: grazing light still counts as lit
parts.say: The small offset keeps grazing light lit. And the shade is a colour of its own, deeper and bluer, not the lit one darkened.

steps.say: The hour is one number. Sky, clouds, mountains and grass all read the same keyed colours, so nothing is repainted.
The second scene is a harbour town in coloured pencil. Its claim is pure code, and it holds. The only file it loads is a skeleton with its clips.

steps.term: Hatch field: a number per vertex the strokes follow
steps.say: The strokes belong to each surface. Every vertex carries two numbers, and strokes run along their level lines, so they never swim.

scenes.credit: the live page, two stroke spacings

steps.say: Only their spacing follows the screen. The shader measures how fast the field changes per pixel and picks a spacing in whole octaves.
Walk in and new strokes fade in half-way between the old ones. Nothing slides. Strokes are only added or taken away.

scenes.title: Where each one puts its style

left.title: Painted Valley
items: A finish over the whole frame
left.say: So the two scenes put their style in different places. The valley paints the screen, and inks only its walker.

right.title: Coloured pencil
items: An outline from depth on everything
right.say: The town draws on the surfaces themselves, and turns light into how hard each stroke is pressed.

scenes.text: Separate light from paint, then decide where the style lives: on the screen, or on the surface.
scenes.say: Separate light from paint, then decide where the style lives: on the screen, or on the surface.

recap: Valley: two tones, ink, a Kuwahara finish
scenes.say: patch is plumbing around your agent. The valley paints the screen, and the town draws on the surfaces. Both are open, so go and walk them. Thanks for watching!
